messages:
maria: FYI a customer on Dedicated reported a sudden p95/p99 tail latency increase after we flipped a new int8 quant profile for their model. They saw p99 jump from ~420ms to ~1.2s.
sam: ack. which pool/region? any model variant info?
maria: eu-west-1, pool-redwood-dedicated-004, model: llama-2-13b-v2 (quant-int8-profile=v4). Canary rollout was at 10%.
ryan: did they enable the new kernel selection too? kernel changes often change tail behavior.
maria: yes — runtime selected new int8 kernels during canary. Metrics attached by customer:

```
- baseline (fp16): p95=380ms, p99=420ms
- after int8-v4 canary: p95=560ms, p99=1.2s
- observed increase mainly for seq_len>1024 and requests with many stop tokens
- no error rate increase, just slower responses
```

sam: interesting. Could be quant-induced slower attention kernels for long sequences or KV-cache miss pattern. Can we repro in our internal canary?
jen: I'm oncall, can run a quick A/B repro on a small subset of traffic. Need exact config: batch sizes, max_new_tokens, prefix cache enabled?
maria: customer config: batch_size=1, max_new_tokens=512, kv_cache=true, streaming=true. Batching disabled at app layer. They also had cache TTL low (30s) so many cold-cache calls.
ryan: cold KV cache + int8 kernels may not have optimized fused paths — fallback to slower path under certain token widths. Also calibration sample size influences kernel choice.

sam: steps I'll do:
1) repro on our dedicated canary with the same model + quant profile v4 + same runtime flags
2) capture perf traces (triton/hostwall + per-kernel counters)
3) force kernel selector to prefer fp16 for sequences >1024 to see if p99 returns to baseline
4) check quant profile metadata: calibration_samples, per-layer scaling, per-head clipping

maria: customer wants quick mitigation; can we temporarily roll them back to fp16 while we investigate?
jen: yes we can pin their routing to the fp16 variant for the next 24h as a mitigation. I can patch their route to model:llama-2-13b-v2:fp16 and push canary revert. Doing that now.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollback-route applied -> model pinned to fp16 for customer-cid-4321 (change id: R-20240301-987)

ryan: re: root cause hypotheses:
- hypothesis A: quantized kernels for some attention sizes use a slower algorithm (non-fused) causing tail latency for long seqs
- hypothesis B: calibration produced outlier scaling that triggers extra de-quant/quant ops at runtime
- hypothesis C: batch/caching heuristics interact with quantized memory layout causing extra memcpy/transpose on hot path

sam: to test A/B:
- run microbench for attention kernels at seq lengths [256,512,1024,1536] under int8-v4 and fp16 and compare per-op p99
- run end-to-end with warm vs cold KV cache

maria: customer asked for a rollback ETA. jen set them to fp16. They're happy for now but want root cause and a safe re-enable plan.
jen: note: we should also check our autoscaler and queue latency — increased kernel latency might amplify queue p99 even at low CPU/GPU util.

ryan: quick findings from internal repro (prelim):
```
- int8-v4 attention kernel p50/p95 ~ same as fp16 at seq<=512
- at seq=1536 int8-v4 p95 ~ +30% and p99 ~ +180% vs fp16
- kernel profiler shows extra fallback to a generic matmul path on certain head counts (not using optimized fused attention)
- quant profile v4 sets per-layer clip thresholds that look aggressive; some layers have near-zero scale causing dequant noise handling code path to run
```

sam: looks like mix of hypothesis A and B. The kernel selector falls back for specific layer shapes when clip thresholds are tight.
ryan: mitigation plan:
- short-term: keep customer pinned to fp16 (done)
- immediate: for next canary, add a runtime guard: if seq_len>1024 or head_count mismatch -> prefer fp16 kernels or fallback to model variant fp16
- medium-term: regenerate quant profile with more calibration samples (increase from 5k -> 50k representative tokens) including long-seq traffic and diverse prompts
- long-term: update kernel selector logic to avoid generic slow path for common long-seq shapes (create optimized kernels or widen fused-kernel coverage)

maria: good. For the medium-term re-calibration, can we run calibration in their dedicated pool so it uses same hardware layout?
ryan: yes, calibration should run on same GPU arch; otherwise scale differences will skew scales. We'll schedule calibration job and ask customer for a small representative prompt corpus.

jen: ops note: we should also add a temporary canary rollout rule: ramp int8 only for seq_len<=512 and users with warm KV cache. That will limit blast radius.

sam: I'll open an internal ticket with perf traces + repro steps and label it p99-quant-tail. Also include a minimal reproducer script and the kernel profiler outputs.

maria: customer-facing note: I'll send the rollback confirmation and ETA for root cause update (24-48h). Thank you all.
ryan: added a quick CLI snippet to force kernel policy for testing:

```
# test repro run
runtimectl run --model llama-2-13b-v2 --quant-profile v4 --override "kernel_policy:prefer_fp16_for_seq>1024" --input-file long_prompts.json
```

jen: leaving this thread. ping me if they see any other anomalies. :thumbsup:
maria: thanks team, closing on our side when ticket created.
